draft.title: The digital divide
card: The digital divide is the gap between people who have good internet access and people who have little or none. Access means a connection that is available, fast enough to use and affordable.
Access differs from one country to another. Wealthier countries tend to have more people online and faster connections than many poorer countries.
Access also differs inside one country. Remote areas and poorer households often have slow, costly or no connection, while cities usually have better options.
Causes can include distance, the high cost of building networks across large areas, and low incomes. Without access, people may find it harder to study, find work or reach services online.
draft.remember: The digital divide is an uneven gap in internet access, both between and within countries.

a.q: Which example shows a digital divide within one country?
opts: A remote Australian town has slow internet, Perth has fast
One country has more internet users than a neighbouring one
A family in Hobart buys a new phone and streams a film
A city library offers free internet to all of its members
a.why: The divide within a country is a gap between places in the same country, here a remote town and a capital city. The comparison of two countries is a gap between countries, not within one.
a.clue: Look for two places in the same country with different access.

b.q: Mia lives on a remote cattle station in the Northern Territory. Her internet is slow and costly, so she struggles to join online classes. Which reason best explains why her access is poor?
opts: Distance makes building fast networks costly for few people
Her family has chosen not to use the internet at home
All people in the Northern Territory have no internet
Fast internet is only found in countries with high incomes
b.why: The card links poor access in remote areas to distance and the high cost of building networks for few users. The option about high-income countries is wrong because the divide also exists inside countries, including wealthy ones.
b.clue: Think about why building networks across large areas is hard.

a.best: A remote Australian town has slow internet, Perth has fast

b.best: Distance makes building fast networks costly for few people
